mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding future equity value.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS average > 5% over the past quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when the FEDFUNDS average exceeds 5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) below 5% are associated with stronger labor market conditions that precede S&P 500 gains over the next 5 trading days, as weaker job market weakness supports risk-on sentiment.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when UNRATE remains below 5% for at least 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, predicting positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as the market anticipates sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% while INDPRO decreases by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative when the HOUST-INDPRO cross is not detected in the 12 months prior.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average for three consecutive months indicates weakening supply chains, which predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as market anticipates production slowdowns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when INDPRO remains below MA for fewer than 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% above its trend, it signals accelerating inflation, which is expected to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors demand higher yields.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when the 3-month CPIAUCSL MA is not above trend + 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets labor market strengthening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by > 0.5pp in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE declines by less than 0.5pp in any month.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending proxies (not available in the given catalog, so this will be omitted) would typically signal demand growth, but using HOUST instead, a 20-day positive return is expected when HOUST rises by 5% month-over-month for two months in a row.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when HOUST growth is not sustained for 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS is above 4% and UNRATE is below 6%, the combination signals a mixed policy signal that is neutral for S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when the combined FEDFUNDS-UNRATE pattern is not detected in the prior 12 months.
